topic: prove causal masking with a falsifiable invariant in a CPU-only mini lab
audience_job: decide, before teaching attention, which claim to make testable first and what a toy result does and does not prove
experiment_variable: the single measured pair: first output with masking against first output without masking
label: LOCAL_RUN

parts:
LLM tutorials should start with a claim you can test.

Change a future token. With causal masking, the first output stays 1.000. Without it, the output shifts from 2.575 to 30.000.

CPU-only toy lab; 5 tests pass.

Source curriculum: https://datawhalechina.github.io/diy-llm/

source_angles.thesis: Learn causal attention by changing a future token and confirming the early output is invariant.
source_angles.evidence: The mini lab passes on Python 3.13.5 on Linux CPU with five standard-library tests.
source_angles.counterexample: A toy one-dimensional Q=K=V example does not represent a trained LLM or a benchmark.
